name: DTVLT
description: Visual language tracking (VLT) has emerged as a cutting-edge research area, harnessing linguistic data to enhance algorithms with multi-modal inputs and broadening the scope of traditional single object tracking (SOT) to encompass video understanding applications. Despite this, most VLT benchmarks still depend on succinct, human-annotated text descriptions for each video. These descriptions often fall short in capturing the nuances of video content dynamics and lack stylistic variety in language, constrained by their uniform level of detail and a fixed annotation frequency. As a result, algorithms tend to default to a "memorize the answer" strategy, diverging from the core objective of achieving a deeper understanding of video content. Fortunately, the emergence of large language models (LLMs) has enabled the generation of diverse text. reputation: A recent benchmark contribution in visual-language tracking that is mainly of interest to the tracking and multimodal understanding community.
notes: Benchmark is derived from existing SOT datasets with LLM-generated annotations, so it is more of a benchmark augmentation than a standalone long-established leaderboard; exact metrics may vary by underlying SOT dataset.
